new_statements.quote: Deze sluiters worden klinkend gemaakt door middel van een steunvocaal, die ze voor wegvallen bewaart, nl. u in het gehele oostelijke taalgebied, behalve Mamboru, a in het gehele westelijke taalgebied en in Mamboru en o in het kodisch. Invloed op het accent, dat als regel valt op de eerste lettergreep van het stamwoord, heeft deze vocaal niet, behalve in Kodi. [...] Het kodisch laat onder invloed van de steunvocaal het accent verspringen, indien de vocaal in de eerste lettergreep kort is, bijv. Mamboru bàndjala, Anakalang bidjalu, Wewewa bòndala, Kodi bandálo, wegbergen [...] Deze verspringing van het accent ook bij aanhechting van grammatische elementen, heeft op het klankbeeld van de zin in het kodisch een belangrijke invloed geoefend.
new_statements.translation: These final consonants are made pronounceable by a support (paragogic) vowel that keeps them from dropping, namely u in the whole eastern language area except Mamboru, a in the whole western area and in Mamboru, and o in Kodi. This vowel has no influence on the accent, which as a rule falls on the first syllable of the stem word, except in Kodi. [...] Under the influence of the support vowel Kodi lets the accent shift if the vowel of the first syllable is short, e.g. Mamboru bàndjala, Anakalang bidjalu, Wewewa bòndala, Kodi bandálo 'to put away' [...] This shifting of the accent, also when grammatical elements are attached, has had an important influence on the sound shape of the sentence in Kodi.

new_statements.relation_note: General Sumbanese accent rule (stem-initial) with Kodi exception; vowel length only under accent; no tone.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Pan-Sumbanese statement: word accent as a rule falls on the first syllable of the stem (stamwoord); the paragogic support vowel (u/a/o) added after stem-final consonants does not attract or move the accent, except in Kodi, where a short first-syllable vowel lets the accent shift rightward onto the following syllable (bandálo, lepéto, haláto), also under affixation. Applicability to Gaura/Nggaura is by inclusion in 'het sumbaas' only; Onvlee groups Nggaura with Kodi dialectally but names only Kodi as the accent exception.
new_statements.exceptions: Kodi accent shift when the first stem vowel is short (paragogic-vowel words); Lamboya deletes unaccented i/u creating clusters (p.166-167); long vowels and à occur only in the accented stem syllable.
new_statements.identity_note: First-hand (Onvlee worked on Sumba 1926-1955 and visited 'het gebied van Ende en Nggaura' 19-26 Aug 1932, p.70). The sketch characterises 'het sumbaas' as a whole, starting from Wewewa with cross-dialect notes; p.165 explicitly places 'het kodisch en het dialect van Nggaura' (= Gaura, ngga1239) together, nearer the eastern group. The accent rule is stated for Sumbanese generally with Kodi (kodi1247) as the single named exception; Nggaura is not named in the accent sentence, so whether Gaura follows the general stem-initial rule or the Kodi accent shift is not stated.

sources.citation: Lovestrand, Joseph. 2021. Languages of Sumba: State of the field. NUSA: Linguistic studies of languages in and around Indonesia 70: 39-60. doi:10.15026/100089
sources.note: Survey, not a description of Gaura. p.43: Gaura is 'a distinct language of West Sumba', known only lexically (Asplund 2010; Gasser 2014); p.52 lists 'the status of Gaura as a separate language' as an open research need. The only stress remark (sec. 4.2, p.48) is about Kodi and Weyewa: 'Weyewa and Kodi have contrastive long consonants, and non-contrastive lengthening of stressed vowels—typically the penultimate syllable (Kuipers 1998:xvii; Lovestrand & Balle 2019)', with Kodi examples [ˈpoːto] 'four', [ˈpotːo]. Nothing on Gaura stress.
